title: Making Your Haircut Last: Practical Care Tips from 3D Cutz in Norwich
description: Simple, practical tips from 3D Cutz in Norwich to keep your haircut looking sharp for longer between visits.

content.heading: Wash and dry with care
paragraphs: Over-washing can strip natural oils and make a cut look limp; aim to wash every other day or as your hair type needs. Use a gentle shampoo and a lightweight conditioner, focusing conditioner on the mid-lengths and ends rather than the roots.

After washing, pat dry with a towel rather than rubbing, then use a blow-drier on a low-to-medium setting if you want volume or hold — directing airflow down the hairshaft helps keep fades and short styles neat.

content.heading: Use the right products, sparingly
paragraphs: Choose styling products that suit your hair’s texture: a light paste or cream for finer hair, matte pomade or wax for thicker hair, and sea-salt sprays for texture. Start with a small amount and build up only if needed to avoid greasy or weighed-down hair.

Apply product to towel-dried hair for a natural finish or to dry hair for stronger hold. Comb or finger-style depending on the look — combs give a cleaner finish for tapered sides, fingers keep textured tops looking fresh.

content.heading: Quick home touch-ups without overdoing it
paragraphs: Keep a trimmer for tidy-ups around the neckline and sideburns between appointments; use a guard and take small amounts off at a time. If you’re not confident with clippers, concentrate on brushing and styling rather than attempting major re-cuts at home.

For longer styles, a pair of scissors and a comb can tame stray ends — again, only remove a few millimetres. When in doubt, book a short tidy-up with your barber rather than risk changing the shape of your cut.

content.heading: Protect your cut overnight and from the weather
paragraphs: Sleep can flatten a haircut; a simple routine like combing hair into place before bed and using a silk or cotton pillowcase reduces friction and helps maintain shape. If you sweat a lot at night, a short freshen-up in the morning will revive the style.

Norwich weather can be wet and blustery, so carry a small styling product or a compact comb to tame flyaways after being outdoors. A lightweight hat can protect a freshly cut style from rain, but remove it carefully to avoid crushing the shape.
